exposure: Kangaroo care (skin-to-skin contact between mother and newborn)
outcome: Emotional communication between mother and child
cohort: 40 full-term newborns randomly divided into an experimental group receiving kangaroo care and a control group receiving conventional care during heel blood collection.
finding: During heel blood collection, skin contact between the mother and child can relieve pain, reduce changes in heart rate, improve neonatal heel blood oxygen saturation, and enhance emotional communication.
